messages:
maria: FYI we just saw a pile of 5xxs on /v1/generate from eu-west ALB. Not normal spike, looks like requests are getting routed to the gpu-pool target group for a different host.

jake: Huh. Any pattern in ClientHello SNI?

maria: Spot-checked tcpdump on alb -> backend. Some ClientHello SNIs are present but have weird padding bytes at the end (0x00).
jake: Could that break ALB listener rule matching? ALB matches SNI for TLS listener rules and then picks target group, right?
henry: ALB listener priority ordering + exact SNI string vs wildcard rules can be surprising. If the SNI bytes don't match expected, it may fall through to default action.
maria: Exactly — a subset of connections with padded SNI are hitting the default TLS listener which is wired to gpu-pool for legacy reasons. That explains the sudden prewarm and GPU utilization spike.
jake: Where is the padding coming from? gRPC clients or our SDK?
maria: Early evidence points to a mobile SDK version 1.14 where our proxy lib pads SNI for ALPN compatibility when using TLS session resumption. Reproducible locally.
henry: Oof. Two urgent questions: 1) how do we stop traffic hitting gpu-pool right now, 2) how to prevent padded SNI from routing incorrectly long-term.
maria: For immediate mitigation I propose adding a listener rule above default that rejects malformed SNI (exact match of expected hostnames) or route to a safe 4xx target group. That way default won't be gpu-pool.
jake: Can we add a rule with condition "if ssl-xyz header SNI != expected -> 403"? ALB supports "If SNI equals" and listener priority. We can create a high-priority rule that matches our expected hosts; fallback rule to a tiny lambdas that returns 404.
henry: Agree. Also quick fix: rewire default action to a neutral bucket instead of gpu-pool. But that requires a config change and might affect other legacy traffic.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Scheduled change: add ALB rule 'protect-sni-mismatch' at priority 5 to eu-west-1 on alb-prod. Pending approvals: @maria @jake.
jake: I started a small runbook for this path. Patch in Terraform is ready:

```hcl
resource "aws_lb_listener_rule" "protect_sni_mismatch" {
  listener_arn = var.alb_tls_listener
  priority     = 5
  action {
    type             = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.null_tg.arn
  }
  condition {
    host_header {
      values = ["api.redwood.ai", "api-eu.redwood.ai"]
    }
  }
}
```

maria: Nice. Null target group returns 404 fast. Do we need canary? I'll run this in eu-west small window.
henry: Also add an alert to catch when target group gpu-pool suddenly gets +50% new connections in <5m. That will help next time.
ops-bot: alert created: ALB-gpu-pool-surge (threshold: +50% conn delta / 5m) -> #eng-oncall.

maria: Postmortem notes: root cause = SDK TLS padding causing SNI mismatch triggering ALB default listener action -> gpu-pool. Mitigations: listener rule + SDK patch + change default listener wiring.
jake: SDK patch posted to repo, PR 432. We should cut a hotfix release for mobile SDK 1.14.1.
henry: Long term we should not route default TLS listener to a costly GPU target group. Keep GPU behind explicit host/port and prefer path-based routing or dedicated subdomain.
maria: Agreed. Also add WAF rule to strip/normalize SNI? Not sure if WAF can operate there but worth investigating.
ops-bot: NOTE: rolling listener change in 2m. If no objections, will apply. @infra-bot please hold rollback window of 15m.
infra-bot: rollback window set: 15 minutes. Snapshotting ALB config.

jake: Applying Terra patch now. I'll monitor connections and 5xx rate.
maria: 2 minutes in — 5xx rate dropping, GPU connections leveling off. Good so far.
henry: Follow-up action items: (1) backfill test for SNI padding in ingress e2e, (2) move gpu-pool off default action, (3) SDK hotfix release, (4) add alert for sudden GPU rx.
maria: I'll own 1 + 3. Jake take 2, Henry take 4.
ops-bot: Change applied successfully. ALB rule 'protect-sni-mismatch' created.
jake: Confirmed: no additional routes hitting gpu-pool since change. 5xxs down to baseline.
maria: Thanks team. Will write runbook and short incident blurb for weekly infra sync.
henry: Good catch. This was a fun one — SNI padding + listener priority chain.
maria: Closing thread, will file postmortem later.
thread_summary: SNI padding in mobile SDK caused ALB listener to fall through to default action which routed to gpu target group; quick fix was adding a high-priority ALB rule to route expected hosts to a null target group and creating alerts; SDK patch and long-term routing changes planned.
